problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=-y\,i+x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =-y\,i+x\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =2{sin}^{2}⁡t+2{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }2\,\text{d}t \\  & =2t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =2(2\pi )-0 \\  & =4\pi \end{aligned}
$$
